articles.title: Dina Thorslund ends Cherneka Johnson's undisputed run to become world champion again after return following miscarriage
articles.summary: Dina Thorslund snatches WBC, WBO, WBA and IBF titles from Cherneka Johnson, winning every round in a unanimous decision in the main event of MVPW-5 in Orlando, Florida; it was an emotional triumph for Thorslund, who returned to the ring following a miscarriage
articles.body:
Dina Thorslund is a world champion again after ending Cherneka Johnson's undisputed run to cap an emotional return to the sport.

Just over a year after vacating her WBC and WBO bantamweight titles because she was pregnant, the undefeated Thorslund fought aggressively from the start to snatch the WBC, WBO, WBA and IBF titles from Johnson, winning every round in a unanimous decision in the main event of MVPW-5 in Orlando, Florida.

Thorslund (25-0, nine KOs) vacated her titles in June 2025, and a month later she announced on social media that she had suffered a miscarriage.

She returned to the ring in January and defeated Almudena Alvarez to capture the vacant WBC interim featherweight title. Then Thorslund, who is 32 years old and from Denmark, dropped back to bantamweight to fight for the undisputed championship.

  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Download Sky Sports app for expert analysis, video and more
  • Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want

The lead-up to Saturday's fight brought more emotional turmoil for Thorslund, whose training partner, Raven Chapman, underwent emergency brain surgery last month after she collapsed during a sparring session in Denmark.

"This has been such an emotional journey for me the last year," Thorslund said, fighting back tears.

"I'm going to take this [title belt] straight back to Raven and say thank you."

Thorslund was in control for the whole fight. Her aggressive combinations put Johnson on the defensive, especially early, and through three rounds, Thorslund had landed 37 punches to Johnson's 14. In the end, Thorslund's non-stop attack of power punches built a 103-62 edge. All three judges scored it 100-90.

Johnson (19-3, eight KOs), who became undisputed champion by knocking out Shurretta Metcalf in July 2025, was unable to utilise her power against Thorslund. Practically every time she connected, Thorslund would respond by landing three or four shots in return.

Stream boxing and more contract-free on NOW

articles.title: Conor Benn vows to wreak havoc against Ryan Garcia to capture WBC welterweight title
articles.summary: Conor Benn has vowed to stop Ryan Garcia and "cause havoc" when they meet for the WBC welterweight title in Las Vegas on September 12; Benn says Garcia's mind games are "just noise" as he targets the belt once held by his father Nigel
articles.body:
Conor Benn has vowed to wreak havoc and stop Ryan Garcia in his quest to become world champion.

Benn will contest his first-career world title fight against WBC welterweight champion Garcia on September 12 in Las Vegas.

Garcia, one of the most high-profile fighters in the sport, has engaged in a war of words with Benn, but the Brit is focused on emphatically silencing the American once and for all.

  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Download Sky Sports app for expert analysis, video and more
  • Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want

"It's all just noise," Benn told Sky Sports. "It doesn't really concern me, doesn't bother me. I'm just coming there to take his title off him.

"I plan on going in there and getting a stoppage, for sure. I'm just going to go in there and do what I do, which is plant one on his chin and try and put him to sleep.

"I prepare diligently hard and always put the work in. I've taken it with both hands and I'm coming in there to cause havoc."

Benn enters the fight off the back of beating Regis Prograis on the undercard of Tyson Fury's comeback fight against Arslanbek Makhmudov in April.

It was at the same venue, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which staged Benn's epic two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Having avenged his first professional defeat at the hands of Eubank Jr in their November 2025 rematch, Benn has set his sights on emulating his father Nigel by winning the WBC belt he held and defended in 11 fights between 1992 and 1995.

"For me to get a world title shot, the prestigious WBC world title, the belt my dad won, it's a blessing," he added.

"That's not my driving factor. My driving factor is to do it for myself. It's for me to prove that I'm one of the best in the world."

Garcia represents a marked step up in the quality of opposition Benn has faced previously, but he is relishing his underdog status.

"I like being the underdog," he said. "I think I perform at my best.

"I think every single one of my fights has led me to this moment. All the pressure I've had early on in my career has prepared me for nights like those at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

"It's prepared me for the noise and the drama and the chaos. So come September 12, it's nothing new, nothing different."

articles.title: Caroline Dubois: Britain's lightweight world champion has 'ingredients' to succeed Katie Taylor as face of boxing, says Nakisa Bidarian
articles.summary: Caroline Dubois will take on Amelia Moore in Birmingham on August 29; the event will be headlined by Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron, who will compete for the unified welterweight world championship; watch MVPW-06 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Caroline Dubois "has the ingredients" to succeed Katie Taylor as one of the biggest stars in boxing, according to Most Valuable Promotions partner Nakisa Bidarian.

Ireland's undisputed super-lightweight world champion Taylor, who turned 40 in July, is set to fight professionally for the final time in an undisputed world super-lightweight title fight against Flora Pili in Dublin on September 5.

A week earlier, lightweight world champion Dubois will seek to maintain her unbeaten record when she defends her WBC and WBO straps against American Amelia Moore, live on Sky Sports on the undercard of Chantelle Cameron's clash with Mikaela Mayer.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

Bidarian told Sky Sports: "For me, the poster fighters of the sport have been Amanda Serrano and Katie Taylor, the two of them have been real trailblazers.

"It's sad to see that arc transition in September for Katie, I think Amanda probably has one more fight left after August 21.

"But women's boxing has never been stronger. It's a young sport, it became an Olympic sport in 2012 where Katie was the beneficiary, and she's created a storied career for herself.

"But we feel good about the future of this sport we feel like we have a roster of athletes. Caroline Dubois is one who I think has the ingredients of Katie Taylor, Amanda Serrano, Laila Ali, Christy Martin and Ronda Rousey all there.

"Of course, the sport's going to miss Katie, of course the ring is going to miss Amanda, but the sport is in a great place."

Salita says Shields is 'definitively No 1'

Undisputed heavyweight champion Claressa Shields is already "definitively" the No 1 fighter in women's boxing, according to her promoter Dmitry Salita.

Two-time Olympic gold medallist Shields has been an undisputed champion in the professional ranks in three weight classes, winning all 18 of her fights.

Asked about Shields' status in the sport amid Taylor's career coming to a close, Salita told Sky Sports earlier this year: "Katie Taylor is a historic figure in boxing, and I've said many times - personally and professionally - that I'm a fan of hers and what she has done for the sport.

"That said, Claressa Shields is definitively the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter in women's boxing today.

"What separates Claressa is not just what she's accomplished in the ring which already stands on its own but the totality of her impact.

"There is something more to being a bona fide superstar than simply being elite in the ring. There's an "it" factor. The ability to headline, to sell out arenas, to create moments, to carry events regardless of the opponent - and Claressa has that.

"She may be the first woman in the history of the sport consistently selling out major arenas regardless of opponent."

Will Shields vs Price happen?

Shields is dropping down from heavyweight in an attempt to become middleweight world champion once more, with the 31-year-old taking on Australian Kaye Scott in Atlanta this weekend.

The fight could be a precursor for a possible blockbuster with Britain's own world champion Lauren Price, who currently holds three of the four welterweight belts.

Talks have previously taken place over Shields and Price meeting at the middleweight, and despite an impasse in negotiations, Salita remains optimistic the fight can happen.

"When Claressa went to Wales, we believed we had the framework of a deal in place, and we're still operating in that spirit," Salita told Sky Sports last month.

"I believe we're close. Claressa is moving down to 160 pounds because she wants to make this fight happen. She's already accomplished so much, but she's always looking for the biggest global fights.

"Lauren is an outstanding fighter and an Olympic gold medallist. This is one of the biggest fights that can be made in women's boxing, and we're confident it will happen.

"Claressa has always done her part to make the biggest fights possible, and this is no different. We're ready to continue the discussions."

Watch MVPW-06 in Birmingham, headlined by Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron and with Caroline Dubois also in action, live on August 29 on Sky Sports. Get Sky Sports or stream boxing with no contract.

articles.title: Jarrell Miller could receive world heavyweight title fight as Murat Gassiev is 'interested' in fighting the American
articles.summary: Jarrell Miller aims to challenge Murat Gassiev for WBA heavyweight belt; Miller could finally receive world title fight following cancelled clash against Anthony Joshua after American tested positive for banned substances in 2019; WBA champion Gassiev is 'interested' in fighting Miller
articles.body:
Jarrell Miller could receive a a WBA world heavyweight title fight against Murat Gassiev.

The WBA recently clarified that Miller is not a mandatory challenger for Gassiev, despite initially announcing this status, but the 38-year-old American still hopes to receive a world title fight against the Russian champion.

Miller confirmed to Sky Sports that a WBA title shot could be next after his points win over Cuban Lenier Pero in April and Gassiev has also revealed that he is open to the fight.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

"Yes, if there is an offer regarding Jarrell Miller, we are of course interested," Gassiev told Sky Sports.

"Furthermore, if Moses Itauma decides to pursue the IBF route, Jarrell Miller will become an official contender for my WBA title, making the fight inevitable for me.

"We are also highly interested in a fight with [WBC champion] Agit Kabayel. If a concrete agreement is reached and this fight begins to materialise, I would gladly sign up for a unification bout.

"It all comes down to the specifics - the offer, the terms, the timing, and the venue. We are targeting fights that make sense both financially and for my career progression."

Moses Itauma is the current WBA No 1 contender, but the unbeaten Brit will fight Filip Hrgovic for the vacant IBF belt on August 19, which should mean that Miller, ranked at No 2 by the WBA, is next in line for Gassiev.

The controversial Brooklyn boxer, nicknamed 'Big Baby', defeated Kingsley Ibeh by split decision in a January fight that went viral after Miller's hairpiece was dislodged in the second round.

Miller could finally receive a shot at a world heavyweight title, more than seven years after his scheduled 2019 fight against Anthony Joshua for the WBA, IBF and WBO titles was cancelled after Miller tested positive for banned substances.

Gassiev was elevated to become the WBA world heavyweight champion after Oleksandr Usyk vacated his WBA, WBC and IBF belts in June.

The 32-year-old defended his WBA title with a sixth-round stoppage win over Peter Kadiru in Moscow last month and is now eager to acquire more world belts.

"It's not just about Kabayel. To put it simply, I want any unification bout available," Gassiev told Sky Sports.

"However, if defending my WBA title against a mandatory challenger becomes the immediate priority, that would be an excellent matchup for me and all boxing fans.

"In that scenario, we will gladly fulfil our mandatory obligations.

"That said, our ultimate goal remains a unification fight. The same applies to the winner of Dubois vs Wardley [for the WBO belt] or Itauma vs Hrgovic.

"We are genuinely interested in any available unification fights."

articles.title: Stevie McKenna is 'locked in' on all-Irish showdown with Callum Walsh after viral KO win, says manager Mike Borao
articles.summary: Stevie McKenna is targeting Irish rival Callum Walsh after knockout of Owen O'Neill went viral on social media; Walsh extended his unbeaten record with points win over Tyler Denny on same bill; McKenna's manager Mike Borao says Walsh fight can be in a major stadium in Ireland or New York
articles.body:
Stevie McKenna is 'locked in' on an all-Irish showdown with Callum Walsh after delivering a dramatic victory in Dublin, says his manager Mike Borao.

McKenna produced a spectacular knockout victory over Owen O'Neill that went viral on social media before his younger brother Aaron was crowned IBF middleweight champion in the main event of Zuffa Boxing 10 on Saturday.

articles.title: Ruby White: Commonwealth Games silver medallist sends message to Sakshi Chaudhary after final defeat in Glasgow
articles.summary: Ruby White wants "revenge" on Sakshi Chaudhary after her defeat in the gold medal bout at the Commonwealth Games; White is targeting gold for Team GB at the 2028 Olympics
articles.body:
Teenage sensation Ruby White only joined the Great Britain Boxing academy in May - by August, she had taken the Commonwealth Games by storm.

The 19-year-old was unbeaten in 71 fights heading into the final, but couldn't extend her incredible streak and take the gold as a 5-0 defeat to Indian Sakshi Chaudhary saw her secure a silver medal in the women's 51kg category in Glasgow.

White's boxing career, though, is just beginning - and as far as she is concerned, the story between her and Chaudhary is far from over.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

"When I'm a little bit more experienced in the senior ranks, I want to get my revenge!

"I was a little bit underprepared for the fight. I had a lot of pressure on me, first multi-sport games, first senior tournament. So I know I can get in there and win - I've just got to change the game plan a little bit more."

Despite her defeat in the final, White prefers to reflect on the positive moments from a tournament she had dreamt of fighting at during childhood.

"I had four very good fights and lost out on the finals. But to reflect back on it, being 19 and to go to the Commonwealth Games after only being selected for GB a couple of months prior, and to come back with silver in my first major tournament, it's amazing.

"I was very upset in the ring after I lost, but I'm on a good path and everything's been amazing ever since.

"It's all experience as an amateur until you get to the Olympics - that when it really matters - but the Commonwealth Games was such an amazing start.

"From seven years old, I worked it out: I always dreamt of going to the 2026 Commonwealth Games and then the 2028 Olympics.

"I'm on the right track to be at such a big tournament. To come away with silver is an achievement, and I'm happy."

White's success has caught the attention of many notable names across British boxing, but the one that stuck out most to her was that of Nicola Adams. The two-time Olympic gold medalist is an idol of White's - and she is hoping to emulate her success for Team GB in 2028.

"Nicola Adams - she surprised me on the radio, and she told me that I'm amazing and I'm on the right track and to keep focused.

"[An olympic gold medal] would be absolutely amazing. I'm just really going to keep training and living life like an athlete. Hopefully I can get to LA [in 2028] and I can bring that gold medal home."

Watch MVPW-06 in Birmingham, headlined by Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron and with Caroline Dubois also in action, live on August 29 on Sky Sports. Get Sky Sports or stream boxing with no contract.

articles.title: Caroline Dubois could face Elif Nur Turhan after rival lightweight world champion signed for Most Valuable Promotions
articles.summary: Turkish world champion Elif Nur Turhan has signed with Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian's Most Valuable Promotions; Caroline Dubois had expressed frustration after being unable to agree terms for a Turhan fight; the Brit could now face Turhan in a WBC, WBO and IBF lightweight title fight
articles.body:
Caroline Dubois could settle her rivalry with Elif Nur Turhan after the Turkish world champion signed for Most Valuable Promotions.

Dubois, who is also signed to MVP, had previously expressed her frustration after being unable to agree a world lightweight unification fight with Turhan, but those negotiations could get simpler now both fighters are aligned in Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian's promotional company.

The unbeaten British champion will defend her WBC and WBO lightweight belts against American Amelia Moore on the Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron bill at the bp pulse LIVE arena in Birmingham on August 29, live on Sky Sports, where every fight on the main card will be a UK vs USA contest.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

Turhan, who is also undefeated in 14 fights, secured the IBF world lightweight title after a stunning stoppage of Beatriz Ferreira and has since retained her title in victories against Gabriella Tellez and Taylah Gentzen.

"Elif Nur Turhan is an undefeated world champion, a tremendous puncher, and now the first Turkish fighter to join the MVP roster," said MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian.

"The Golden Turkish Warrior is one of the most exciting fighters in boxing given her immense punching power and her relentless aggressive, pressure heavy style.

"Signing Elif will allow us to make some of the most exciting fights in boxing. We look forward to welcoming Elif to MVP and giving her the platform to become one of the biggest stars in women's boxing as we continue building MVPW into the premier global home for the sport."

articles.title: Damar Thomas unfazed by Anthony Joshua comparisons as Commonwealth Games gold medallist chases 'own legacy' ahead of LA Olympics
articles.summary: Damar Thomas followed in the footsteps of Joe Joyce, Frazer Clarke and Delicious Orie at the Commonwealth Games but has since dismissed Anthony Joshua comparisons; the 21-year-old super-heavyweight is targeting success at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles
articles.body:
Commonwealth Games gold medallist Damar Thomas wants to create his "own legacy" after being compared to former Team GB super-heavyweight stars following his triumph in Glasgow.

The boxer followed in the footsteps of Joe Joyce, Frazer Clarke and Delicious Orie when he beat India's Narender Berwal via unanimous decision to win gold in the super-heavyweight category.

Standing at 6ft 6in, Thomas has earned inevitable comparisons with Anthony Joshua and represents one of the great hopes for the future of British heavyweight boxing.

The 21-year-old, who is targeting success at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, is unfazed by such comparisons and insists he is focused on his own development.

"Yeah, it's a great feeling [to win gold]. I managed to add my name to the British heavyweights that won the Commonwealth [gold]," he said.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

"Hopefully in LA I'll be able to add my name to those great heavyweights that managed to get Olympic gold.

"I'm just in my own race at the minute and taking it in my own strides. I'm not comparing myself to anyone. I'm doing everything at my own pace, which is great. What I want to do is create my own legacy, which is a good feeling."

Thomas demonstrated significant boxing IQ in his 5-0 victory over Berwal, marking his 11th consecutive win in a run that extends back to November.

"My main asset is my feet and my speed," Thomas said.

"That's what works for me with these heavyweights, because a lot of these heavyweights rely on one shot. I don't rely on that, so it's great."

While Thomas' main ambition for now is to remain amateur and win gold in LA, he has his sights set on becoming a professional after the games in 2028.

"First, I want to tick off that box with LA. I'm taking one tournament at a time," he added.

"It's a marathon, not a sprint. And I'm just taking everything at my own pace.

"The main goal is the Olympics. Until then, I'm thinking about Olympics and nothing else. But after the Olympics, I'll definitely turn professional."

articles.title: Craig Richards vs Radivoje Kalajdzic, Lee Cutler vs Louis Greene added to Johnny Fisher boxing bill at Copper Box Arena
articles.summary: Zuffa Boxing adds Craig Richards-Radivoje Kalajdzic and Lee Cutler-Louis Greene bouts to Copper Box Arena bill headlined by Johnny Fisher's latest heavyweight fight; watch it all live on Sky Sports on September 26
articles.body:
British former world title challenger Craig Richards will take on Radivoje Kalajdzic in a 10-round light heavyweight showdown, while Lee Cutler faces Louis Greene in a middleweight clash, on Zuffa Boxing's Johnny Fisher bill at London's Copper Box Arena.

Richards vs Kalajdzic will serve as the chief support bout to the 10-round heavyweight main event featuring Fisher at Zuffa Boxing 11 on September 26, live on Sky Sports.

An opponent for 'The Romford Bull' will be announced in the coming days.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

Richards (20-4-1, 13 KOs) is a world-ranked former British champion who fought Dmitry Bivol for the WBA light-heavyweight title in 2021. He won his two most recent fights in 2025, including a knockout win over Dan Azeez last December.

The fight will mark the first time hard-hitting, Serbian-born Kalajdzic (30-3, 22 KOs) has fought outside North America as a professional. The 35-year-old's last fight was a seventh-round knockout victory against Oleksandr Gvozdyk in February.

The Copper Box Arena bill will also feature a 10-round middleweight showdown between British boxers Cutler and Greene.

Cutler beat Stevie McKenna on points when they fought in December 2024, marking the only professional defeat for Ireland's KO king so far.

Cutler's last fight saw him stop Aaron Sutton in his hometown of Bournemouth in three rounds, while Greene - a former Commonwealth super-welterweight champion - earned a points decision win over Daniel Buciuc in Dublin last week.

Decorated British amateur Kayla Allen is also fighting as part of her professional debut after becoming the first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing.

Alex MacMillan, Leon Hughes and Fred Pullen, who is also turning professional, are also on the London bill.

Richards: My story isn't written yet - the time is now

Craig "Spider" Richards speaking on Sky Sports News:

"It's a very exciting fight. Everyone knows Kalajdzic can punch, I can punch, we've both been two fighters who haven't shied away from competition.

"We've been in with everyone, we've mixed it, we both probably want to push on now towards that world title and I feel like it's a great opportunity.

"UK vs USA - that mix always goes down well! I'm up for it, I'm excited and I think this is now going to be the best version of me going into the new chapter and I get to go and display what I'm about.

"I feel like my story is not written yet and I feel like I need to write it now.

"The problem we had before is that a lot of opponents were turning [a fight with] me down, saying 'he's a hard fight, he's a long night in the office'.

"Zuffa doesn't allow you to do that, and that means I can get some activity. I can go out there and make a statement."

Watch Johnny Fisher's next fight at London's Copper Box Arena, on Saturday September 26, live on Sky Sports. Get Sky Sports or stream boxing with no contract.

articles.title: Prichard Colon: Boxer dies aged 33 more than a decade after suffering severe brain injury
articles.summary: Prichard Colon suffered brain haemorrhage in fateful 2015 fight against Terrel Williams that left the Puerto Rican fighter in a coma for 221 days and in a vegetative state for the rest of his life
articles.body:
Boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33, 11 years after suffering a severe brain injury during a fight, his father has confirmed.

Colon, then aged 23, collapsed in his dressing room after his October 2015 fight against Terrel Williams in Virginia.

The Puerto Rican suffered a brain haemorrhage and was rushed to hospital, where he underwent emergency surgery that left him in a coma for 221 days.

Colon spent the rest of his life in a vegetative state, unable to walk and requiring 24-hour care.

"Good morning, my people. I'm sorry to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world," Colon's father, Richard, wrote on Facebook.

"He is now in a better world. I did everything I could to fulfil his desire and his dream of bringing him to Puerto Rico on holiday, as he wanted, but it couldn't happen.

"Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. Please keep us in your prayers as much as you can."

Colon, a former super welterweight, was undefeated in 16 fights as a professional before facing Williams.

He was disqualified after removing his gloves at the end of round nine before his condition deteriorated and he was rushed to hospital.

The World Boxing Organization posted a tribute to Colon on social media, saluting his warrior spirit until the end.

"The WBO family mourns the passing of Prichard Colón, whose courage, strength and fighting spirit transcended the ring," it wrote on X.

"His greatest fight became a testament to resilience and the unwavering love of his family."

articles.title: Claressa Shields vs Lauren Price is 'mega event' that 'belongs in United States' says the American's promoter Dmitriy Salita
articles.summary: Claressa Shields can reclaim the WBC and WBA middleweight belts when she faces Kaye Scott in Atlanta in the early hours of Sunday morning; Shields is then expected to fight Britain's Lauren Price and the American's star's promoter says the Welsh boxer should come to the USA for the fight
articles.body:
Claressa Shields versus Lauren Price is a 'mega' fight that 'belongs in the United States', says the American star's promoter Dmitriy Salita.

Shields can add another world title triumph to her long list of achievements when she fights Kaye Scott for the WBC and WBA middleweight belts in the early hours of Sunday morning.

Price, who is a unified welterweight champion, has welcomed a future clash between two Olympic gold medallists but Salita believes Shields should receive home advantage for the middleweight fight.

  • Craig Richards returns on Johnny Fisher bill at Copper Box
  • Stevie McKenna 'locked in' on Callum Walsh clash
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

"Claressa came down to middleweight to make the biggest fights possible," Salita told Sky Sports.

"She flew to see Lauren Price fight and I invited Price to be ringside for Claressa's fight on Saturday night.

"We want to make this a mega-event, and I believe that fight belongs in the United States.

"That being said, we love the UK and another fight there is certainly not out of the question. It's an incredible time for women's boxing."

But Shields must firstly overcome Scott in Atlanta to become a middleweight world champion for a third time.

"Scott is ready and highly motivated, and Claressa always comes to make a statement," said Salita.

"I expect an electric fight at State Farm Arena. It will be the first time a woman has headlined a combat sports event in this historic building, and we expect a multi-figure gate.

"That's a tremendous milestone for Claressa, women's boxing and the sport as a whole."

Shields has proclaimed herself as the GWOAT, meaning the Greatest Woman Of All Time, and she can strengthen her claim as the world's no 1 female fighter, with Katie Taylor set to retire next month.

"Every one of Claressa's fights is historic," said Salita.

"This will be only the second time in more than 120 years of boxing that a fighter has come down from heavyweight to become middleweight world champion.

"Claressa is a generational talent and a legacy-defining champion, and August 15 will be another history-making night."
paragraphs:
Claressa Shields versus Lauren Price is a 'mega' fight that 'belongs in the United States', says the American star's promoter Dmitriy Salita.

Shields can add another world title triumph to her long list of achievements when she fights Kaye Scott for the WBC and WBA middleweight belts in the early hours of Sunday morning.

Price, who is a unified welterweight champion, has welcomed a future clash between two Olympic gold medallists but Salita believes Shields should receive home advantage for the middleweight fight.

articles.title: ONE Championship: Nico Carrillo knocks out Zhou Jiaqiang in kickboxing debut on ONE Fight Night 46
articles.summary: Nico Carrillo knocks out Chinese star Zhou Jiaqiang in the second round of their featherweight tussle at Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium, proving that his Muay Thai skills brilliantly translated to the kickboxing
articles.body:
Nico Carrillo made a statement winning debut in kickboxing as he stopped Zhou Jiaqiang in the second round at ONE Fight Night 46 in Bangkok.

The newly crowned ONE featherweight Muay Thai world champion answered questions over how his renowned knockout power would translate from four-ounce gloves to the kickboxing ranks by overwhelming Zhou at Lumpinee Stadium on Saturday morning.

Carrillo had to weather a bright start from the Chinese striker, who enjoyed success with sharp combinations and slick movement during the opening round.

But the Scot shifted through the gears in the second after being caught with a front kick to the face.

Responding instantly, Carrillo unleashed a barrage of punches and forced Zhou onto the back foot as the contest turned into a firefight.

The 27-year-old gradually broke down his opponent with heavy shots to the head and body, a series of left hooks to the midsection proving particularly damaging.

With Zhou trapped in the corner and running on empty, Carrillo closed the show with another sustained assault.

The Chinese fighter eventually fell to the canvas and was unable to beat the count, prompting the referee to wave off the contest at 2:47 of the second round.

The victory was the 30th of Carrillo's professional career and an ideal start to his pursuit of world titles in two sports.

articles.title: Claressa Shields stops Kaye Scott to reclaim WBC and WBA middleweight belts
articles.summary: Claressa Shields reclaimed the WBC and WBA middleweight titles with a sixth-round stoppage of Kaye Scott in Atlanta and is now expected to face Britain’s Lauren Price; Shields' promoter believes the Welsh fighter should travel to the US for the potential showdown
articles.body:
Claressa Shields stopped Kaye Scott in the sixth round to reclaim the WBC and WBA middleweight belts in Atlanta.

Shields had moved down from heavyweight to middleweight for the bout and in the process, became a middleweight world champion for a third time.

The fight was under Shields' control throughout, with the crucial moments coming in the sixth round when the 42-year-old Scott was dropped before being subjected to a barrage of punches against the ropes.

  • Craig Richards returns on Johnny Fisher bill at Copper Box
  • Stevie McKenna 'locked in' on Callum Walsh clash
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

The onslaught continued, prompting Scott's corner to throw multiple towels into the ring, bringing an end to the contest after one minute and 38 seconds of the sixth round.

With the victory, Shields improves to 19-0, further strengthening the self-proclaimed GWOAT - meaning Greatest Woman of All Time - and her claim to being the world's No 1 female fighter, particularly with Katie Taylor set to retire.

"It was a hard camp," Shields said. "I always tell myself that everything is easy work, but it was a really hard camp.

"I cut 38 pounds. I started 14 weeks ago at 198 and got down to 160. It was the most disciplined I've been since the Olympics, I feel like.

"She was stronger than I thought. She was very strong. I knew that, with the amount of weight I'd cut, I didn't want to exert too much energy early.

"I was trying to make sure I could deal with her strength and not get caught with anything crazy, because I'm not as strong as I feel at 175."

Lauren Price is now Shields' preferred opponent at 160lbs, with the American saying she wants the fight to take place between December and January.

It is a fight that Price has welcomed, but the American star's promoter, Dmitriy Salita, believes the "mega" event "belongs in the United States".

"Claressa came down to middleweight to make the biggest fights possible," Salita told Sky Sports.

"We want to make this a mega-event, and I believe that fight belongs in the United States.

"That being said, we love the UK, and another fight there is certainly not out of the question. It's an incredible time for women's boxing."

articles.title: Claressa Shields vs Lauren Price talks are 'ongoing' after American star reclaimed world middleweight titles in Atlanta
articles.summary: Claressa Shields became world middleweight champion for a third time after a sixth-round stoppage of Kaye Scott in Atlanta; promoter Dmitriy Salita says talks are 'ongoing' for Shields to face Lauren Price who is a unified world welterweight champion and a fellow Olympic gold medallist
articles.body:
Negotiations for a Claressa Shields vs Lauren Price fight are ongoing after the American star reclaimed two world middleweight titles on Saturday.

Shields took back WBC and WBA belts with a ruthless sixth-round stoppage of Kaye Scott as the unbeaten Michigan fighter became a middleweight world champion for a third time.

Price, the unified welterweight champion, could be the next opponent for Shields and the American's promoter Dmitriy Salita is keen to finalise terms for a battle between two Olympic gold medallists.

  • Shields stops Scott to regain world middleweight titles
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

"We're working on it as we speak," Salita told Sky Sports.

"Our intention is to make the fight. Based on my understanding, we have agreed to all the requests from [Price's promotional team] BOXXER and Lauren's side.

"I invited Lauren and her team to the fight because my relationship with the fighters we promote, and certainly with Claressa, is that they know all the moving parts and are business partners in making these decisions.

"I wanted Lauren and Claressa to have an opportunity to sit down together and see if there was anything outstanding. Claressa is extremely intelligent and very experienced in making big fights, and I'm sure Lauren is sharp as well.

"Unfortunately, they weren't able to make it, but the conversations are ongoing and we want to make the fight."

Shields has also been linked with a fight against WBO and IBF world middleweight champion Tamm Thibeault and fellow American Mikaela Mayer, who faces Chantelle Cameron in a unified world super-welterweight title fight in Birmingham on August 29, live on Sky Sports.

"Claressa wants to fight the best and be part of the biggest, most impactful events - that's always been clear," said Salita.

"There are a few other conversations taking place in case the Lauren Price fight doesn't come together.

"We'll make a decision soon, but whatever is next, the goal is for it to be another legacy-making moment for Claressa and for boxing."

Shields attracted a huge crowd to State Farm Arena in Atlanta, including some of the biggest names in boxing and music, and Salita believes his fighter's reputation has transcended sport.

"It was incredible. We were getting calls and requests from some of the biggest stars in hip-hop, music, boxing and culture right up until the final bell," he said.

"Usher, Floyd Mayweather, Kevin Gates, Terence Crawford - and the list goes on. The atmosphere was electric.

"It was a special night in a packed arena and a real reflection of Claressa's star power and how far her reach has grown beyond boxing."

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua negotiations enter critical week with ongoing talks about staging fight in New York
articles.summary: Tyson Fury has teased an Anthony Joshua fight announcement on social media; The British heavyweight rivals are yet to finalise terms for a fight; Anthony Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn is keen for the bout to be held in the UK but New York is now being discussed as a location
articles.body:
Negotiations for the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight have entered a 'critical week' with talks ongoing about staging the heavyweight clash in New York.

The British stars are set to finally share the ring this year, although an official announcement has been delayed over discussion about the location of the fight, with Madison Square Garden now emerging as the likely venue.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has revealed how the original fight contract stipulated that the bout would be staged in the UK, but fresh negotiations are taking place amid growing optimism that the blockbuster battle will be confirmed for later this year.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

Frank Smith, Matchroom Boxing CEO, told Sky Sports: "It will disappointing for it not to be in the UK, but at the same time if it means seeing the fight, we all want to see that fight happen. Let's see how things play out.

"There's obviously been suggestions and discussions about New York. AJ has fought there before. AJ has fought all around the world. We're following the terms of what we signed up to right now, which is a fight in the UK. That is what we signed up to and when the fight was announced in March, April time, the fight was signed, those were the terms we signed up for.

"They are the conversations really that are taking place right now. MSG is a proposed venue that they would like to look at, i.e The Ring Magazine, Saudi delegation, so let's see.

"I think November is possible. Later in November is possible, but again the next seven to 10 days, a lot of progress has got to be made in order to make that happen to get [fighters] into camp to give yourself that eight to 10 week period, a dedicated camp away from all the promotional obligations.

"The pressure is on over the next week to get it done."

Asked if the next week is 'critical', Smith added: "I would say 100 per cent. It's never easy putting timeframes on things but when it comes to the date of it actually happening, the next week or so we need to get things together."

Both fighters sharpened their skills in warm-up fights last month as Fury sealed a seventh-round stoppage of Mariusz Wach before Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga after recovering from an early knockdown.

"We're all focused on making it happen," said Smith. "We're all focused on getting the final details together but some work still to be done.

"Lots of discussions ongoing. Lots of conversations happening right now. I'm confident that the fight will happen.

"I'm very confident we will see that fight and AJ will knock out Tyson Fury this year."

Fury teases AJ fight 'It's the one you've all been waiting for!

Fury had earlier teased that a fight announcement was 'imminent', a few hours after Netflix had run a promotional video during its WWE coverage with the closing tagline that the event was 'coming soon.'

Speaking on his official Instagram, Fury had said: "Everything is going well. I've got some big news going to be dropped very soon. All is good in the hood. Big fight on the horizon.

"It's the one you've all been waiting for about to be announced imminently, so stay tuned."

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua Announcement Teased amid Rumors of Date  & Location for Superfight
articles.summary: More information on a bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua appears to be on the way soon.
articles.body:
More information on a bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua appears to be on the way soon.

Fury teased an announcement for the fight on social media on Tuesday.

"I've got some big news going to be dropped very, very soon," Fury said in a post on Instagram (h/t ESPN's James Regan ). "All is good in the hood. Big fight on the horizon. It's the one you've all been waiting for. About to be announced imminently, so stay tuned. Get up."

Fury and Joshua have signed to fight each other, with November being a target date. A venue for the fight has not been officially announced, though Charlotte Daly of the Daily Mail reported that Madison Square Garden is "understood to have been agreed as the venue."

Daly also noted that Joshua and his promoter pushed for the fight to take place in the United Kingdom, but New York was ultimately decided to be the location.

Fury has split his last four fights but is coming off back-to-back wins against Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach. Joshua has likewise won his last two fights, beating Jake Paul last year and Kristian Prenga in July.

articles.title: Joe Gallagher gives cancer update: 'After January setback, I have an operation in September to get rid of this'
articles.summary: Manchester boxing coach Joe Gallagher speaks on latest episode of Toe2Toe Sky Sports Boxing podcast; Gallagher reveals after receiving all-clear from cancer in September, scans in January showed it had returned to his liver; Having undergone chemo, he will have operation in September
articles.body:
Boxing trainer Joe Gallagher has revealed his cancer returned in January, but after responding well to chemotherapy he has an operation in September with hopes of getting the all-clear again.

Speaking as a guest on the latest episode of the Toe2Toe Sky Sports Boxing podcast, esteemed Manchester coach Gallagher was previously diagnosed with stage four bowel and liver cancer, undergoing chemotherapy and a major operation.

He received the all-clear in September last year and was well enough to accompany his fighter Mikie Tallon to Las Vegas to box in a mid-week show ahead of Canelo Alvarez vs Terence Crawford.

But scans in January revealed the cancer had returned to his liver.

"2026 has been a bumpy road. It was a right kick in the nuts at the beginning of the year," Gallagher tells Sky Sports.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

"In September, I got given the all clear on the plane to Vegas, and then I went in back in January for something to do with my heart - believe it or not, I have a heart! - I went for scans and then they came back and they said: 'Listen the cancer has come back to your liver.'

"They said it was inoperable at first, and then there was chance of it being operable, but I had to do a load of chemo to shrink it. So I've gone through seven cycles, and it was a lot more aggressive.

"The cocktail of chemo was huge. Obviously, you could see me losing my hair and everything else.

"I've been doing that, coming through it all, so now I'm going to have an operation in September to get rid of this.

"There's four areas of the liver that has got cancer, three of them can be cut out, one of them they've got to burn it out, but that one is sitting on a main artery that's carrying blood from the feet to the heart.

"That's the one that needed to shrink a little bit, which it has.

"The consultant is very matter of fact, which they have to be. He said I needed to rest.

"But I was just so annoyed because I thought: '2026, here we go, I've got a great team of talent coming through.' And then I thought: 'Oh my God.'

"But we've still worked on. I was in the gym yesterday.

"Everyone knows I'm not available in September. But I'll be back for the beginning of October, hopefully."

Tallon: I have ambitions of fighting on Joshua vs Fury undercard

Mikie Tallon, also speaking to Toe2Toe Sky Sports Boxing podcast, said:

"I know just as much as everyone else [regarding Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua]. I've seen Netflix put a promo out on the WWE last night or something like that.

"It'll be great. Joshua vs Fury. A mega fight.

"So, I'll keep my fingers crossed. If I could get on the card, I would. Definitely.

"Before the Fury [undercard] fight, that was my first stoppage when I did him [Argentinian Olympian Leandro Jose Blanc] in the first round with a body shot, Joe [Gallagher] was making montages and little clips of all the fighters years ago.

"Like Callum Smith, Beefy Smith, Scott Quigg, Anthony Crolla, Paul Butler, Marcus Morrison - all them stopping people with body shots.

"I said to myself, the next time he's going to put me in one of those videos. And then after we got that stoppage win, I was like: 'You can add me to one of those videos now, Joe!'

Mikie Tallon, also speaking to Toe2Toe Sky Sports Boxing podcast, said:

"I know just as much as everyone else [regarding Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua]. I've seen Netflix put a promo out on the WWE last night or something like that.

"It'll be great. Joshua vs Fury. A mega fight.

"So, I'll keep my fingers crossed. If I could get on the card, I would. Definitely.

"Before the Fury [undercard] fight, that was my first stoppage when I did him [Argentinian Olympian Leandro Jose Blanc] in the first round with a body shot, Joe [Gallagher] was making montages and little clips of all the fighters years ago.

"Like Callum Smith, Beefy Smith, Scott Quigg, Anthony Crolla, Paul Butler, Marcus Morrison - all them stopping people with body shots.

"I said to myself, the next time he's going to put me in one of those videos. And then after we got that stoppage win, I was like: 'You can add me to one of those videos now, Joe!'

articles.title: ONE Fight Night 48: Paul Elliott eyes 'life-changing' world title shot with win over Shamil Erdogan
articles.summary: ONE Fight Night 48 on Friday, October 2 - live on Sky Sports - also features Luke Lessei versus Charlie Guest in a hugely important Muay Thai match in terms of featherweight title picture - as the winner could push for a crack at Nico Carrillo's belt
articles.body:
Paul Elliott is eyeing a 'life-changing' world title shot should he come through his ONE Championship heavyweight bout with Shamil Erdogan, but stopped short of promising another record-equalling knockout.

The Middlesbrough-born fighter takes on Erdogan at ONE Fight Night 48 on Friday, October 2 - live on Sky Sports - with the winner possibly earning a shot at the vacant ONE heavyweight MMA world title, which was last held by Anatoly Malykhin before he retired.

Elliott holds an 8-2 record, earning all of his wins by knockout, entering the history books in June when he tied the fastest knockout in ONE history by stopping Regan Upshaw in six seconds.

  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

"I'm probably going to struggle to match that I think," Elliott told Sky Sports. "Don't get me wrong, as soon as the bell goes, I do try to finish fights - I'm known for doing that.

"But he's obviously aware of that now, so he's probably going to keep himself in a defensive position past 10 seconds at least."

The 34-year-old has won his last four fights in a row, but is now set for his stiffest challenge yet in the form of the Erdogan, two years his senior who was born in Russia but who now represents Turkey.

"I think it's going to be a great fight," Elliott said. "He's super skilful, I'm super skilful.

"Because he's quite well-rounded, I think it will probably go past round one.

"He's pretty resilient, so although I'm very explosive and fast, he's technically sound. It might be a bit of a chess match.

"He's probably going to try and wrestle me. I could be wrong, but I think that's what he's going to try and do."

He added: "At heavyweight, we all know one shot can change it.

"We'll both be super switched on and I think it will probably be a razor-thin win for one of us.

"I don't think it's going to be a draw, I don't think it's going to go the distance.

"I think one of us is going to leave with our hand raised and it's going to be before the final bell.

"I believe that whoever wins this will get a title shot."

Elliott labelled Canada's Ben Tynan as "the only name that probably springs to mind" as a potential opponent for the vacant ONE heavyweight belt were he to get past Erdogan.

"It would be a huge achievement to fight for a title, let alone win one," he said. "It would massively change my life.

"Fighting for One Championship alone has definitely elevated my life, it's a great thing.

"It has definitely put me on the map in the world of fighting. Even with the casual fans; I'm getting noticed a lot more now, which is cool.

"But to be world champion, that's going to go down in history. It's the pinnacle.

"Quite frankly, if I can do that it will be the best thing I've ever done in my life."

What else is on ONE Fight Night 48 card?

ONE Fight Night 48 on October 2 - live on Sky Sports - also features Luke Lessei versus Charlie Guest in a hugely important Muay Thai match in terms of the featherweight title picture - as the winner could push for a crack at Nico Carrillo's belt.

Guest is also English, holding a 38-15 record. He made his ONE debut in June, beating Sam Fitzgerald by second-round TKO.

American Lessei is 9-3 and is coming off a July win over Mohamed Younes Rabah.

articles.title: Johnny Fisher's opponent confirmed as Michael Pirotton ahead of return of 'The Romford Bull' on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Johnny Fisher returns against Belgian opponent Michael Pirotton at The Copper Box Arena on September 26, live on Sky Sports, Fisher has vowed to deliver an explosive victory; Craig Richards faces Radivoje "Hot Rod" Kalajdzic and Lee Cutler collides with Louie Greene on the undercard
articles.body:
Johnny Fisher's opponent has been confirmed as Michael Pirotton ahead of the eagerly awaited return of the 'Romford Bull' next month.

The British heavyweight (14-1, 12 KOs) makes his Zuffa Boxing debut against Belgium's Pirotton in the 10-round main event, live on Sky Sports on Saturday, September 26.

Fisher ended the year with a stoppage win over Ivan Balaz in December, putting his career back on track after a rematch loss to David Allen in May.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

Pirotton (12-2, 6 KOs) lies in wait next, with Fisher telling Sky Sports: "I'm excited, but I'm also driven and determined.

"The next fight is always the hardest fight, and everyone I fight is a dangerous opponent because they're getting onto this show with Sky Sports, Zufa, with the Romford Bull Army there.

"It's a golden ticket for Michael Pirotton, but it's also my golden ticket because if I win, I get to go on to bigger and better things. I've got ambitions in this game."

Pirotton made his professional debut in 2019 and won his first 10 fights. After dropping a pair of decisions to unbeaten foes in 2025, he rebounded this year with two stoppage victories.

He has never previously been knocked down, but Fisher is hoping to change that.

"You want to get the knockout, you want to get the stoppage, but I've always said from the beginning of my career, I've got to win by whatever cost - the win is the most important thing." he said.

"But with my power, my strength, my explosivity, of course I can draw a knockout or draw a stoppage.

"Once I get someone hurt, I know I can finish them. I can smell when someone's feeling it or in trouble.

Fisher added: "I'm very very excited to show people what I can do. You haven't seen the best version of the Romford Bull yet. We're going to try and show that on September 26."

Fisher vs. Pirotton tops a bill that also features a 10-round light heavyweight co-main event between Craig "Spider" Richards, Radivoje "Hot Rod" Kalajdzic, and British middleweights Lee Cutler (16-2, 8 KOs) and Louis Greene (19-4, 12 KOs) squaring off in a 10-rounder.

Welterweight Alex MacMillan (4-0, 3 KOs) and light heavyweight Leon Hughes (5-0, 4 KOs) will see action in separate six-rounders, while lightweights Kayla Allen and Fred Pullen will make their respective professional debuts.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Contract delays raise doubts, says Fury's manager Spencer Brown
articles.summary: Tyson Fury's manager Spencer Brown admits concerns are growing over whether the Anthony Joshua fight will happen as delays continue; Brown says Fury is "ready to rock and roll" but fears fans could lose interest if an announcement is not made soon
articles.body:
Tyson Fury's manager Spencer Brown has admitted there are growing concerns Anthony Joshua could yet walk away from their long-awaited heavyweight showdown.

On Tuesday, Netflix released a trailer during its coverage of WWE RAW labelled Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua - Coming Soon, fuelling speculation that an announcement on the blockbuster British clash could be imminent.

But the date and venue for the fight have yet to be confirmed, with negotiations continuing and Fury's camp becoming increasingly frustrated by the delay.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

Fury expressed concerns over whether the Joshua fight would materialise after beating Mariusz Wach in Thailand in his final warm-up fight in July.

Speaking exclusively to Dev Sahni, Brown revealed the prolonged wait for the fight to be finalised was raising fresh doubts over whether it would happen at all.

"Everybody's got a bit of doubt in their mind," he said. "There's reasons you could think that.

"If you'd asked me a week ago, I'd have said no, but now it's a little bit concerning that things haven't progressed down the line. We need to get this fight on."

New York's Madison Square Garden appears to be the frontrunner to host the fight despite Joshua's insistence that the contest takes place in the UK.

Brown confirmed every effort had been made to stage the fight at Wembley Stadium but conceded those hopes were fading, while warning further delays risked damaging public interest in the event.

"You can't keep flogging a dead horse, can you?" he added. "We've been flogging a dead horse for months now.

"We've waited and waited to do it at Wembley. The hope is fading that it's going to be at Wembley.

"A decision must be made. Let's get the fight on wherever it is, whether it's in Timbuktu or whether it's in Wembley Stadium.

"We just want to get it announced. People are getting bored. We're in danger of really boring people."

Fury 'ready to rock and roll'

Brown insisted Fury is ready to begin training camp immediately, with the former heavyweight champion eager to finally lock in a date for the Joshua fight.

"All I can say is that we're ready to rock and roll, we're ready to fight," Brown said.

"Tyson wants to get into camp this week so we're looking for an announcement this week. We want it done. We want to get it out of the way.

"I think it's all ready to go. The bags are packed. All the team are ready to go. We've pre-empted everything. We're just waiting for the go button."

Brown said Fury's confidence that the fight would happen had increased in recent weeks, although he acknowledged uncertainty remains while the final details are still being worked through.

"It's gone further and further and further. I'm sitting there convincing him that it's going to happen," Brown said.

"I think he's now more confident of it happening, a lot more confident than what we was. But he's going to fight whatever happens."

articles.title: Amanda Serrano seeks historic knockout of Lucrecia Manzur in final act of illustrious boxing career
articles.summary: Amanda Serrano says breaking the women’s boxing knockout record and securing a 50th career win would fulfil her final remaining goals before retirement; the unified featherweight champion also hinted at a potential return to MMA after her August 21 fight with Lucrecia Manzur
articles.body:
Amanda Serrano has set her sights on securing one final piece of history before bringing the curtain down on her illustrious boxing career.

The reigning unified featherweight world champion faces Argentina's Lucrecia Manzur on August 21 in California, looking to secure her 50th professional victory.

Serrano can also set a new all-time women's boxing knockout record if she halts Manzur inside the distance for the 33rd stoppage of her career.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

And Serrano says pulling clear of Christy Martin, with whom she currently shares the record of 32 KOs, would leave nothing more for her to achieve in the sport.

"This is definitely my last goal," Serrano, the seven-weight world champion, told Sky Sports.

"That's what gets me up in the morning, these little goals. It motivates me. This is the last one, breaking the record, the 50th win, my last farewell one, and that's it.

"I believe I have accomplished everything I wanted to when I decided to take on boxing."

Manzur coming to 'beat my head off'

Serrano is one of women's boxing's most decorated stars and represents a prized scalp for up-and-coming fighters.

The Puerto Rican is prepared for Manzur to attempt to "beat her head off" but is confident she has the skills to deliver a historic viral moment fitting of the fight's airing on TikTok.

"This is a special fight for me, especially being on TikTok, where it can be a viral moment," Serrano added. "I guarantee the 50th win is coming, but we're working on the 33rd knockout.

"Manzur is a very tough fighter. She's a Latina like me, she's Argentinian, she's going to come forward.

"The difference now with these girls, this new generation, is that they come in different. They come in to make a name for themselves in this sport.

"I know she's going to try to come and beat my head off, but she's never fought someone like me. We've been working really hard for the knockout, and I believe it can come."

Could Serrano return to the cage?

The Manzur fight might spell the end of Serrano's boxing career, but perhaps not the end of her involvement in combat sports, with the 37-year-old open to building on her three-fight MMA career.

"Well, I am undefeated in MMA," Serrano said. "I'm 2-0-1, with two submissions.

"I love the knockouts, but I think I love submissions a lot more. It's a lot more fun to get a submission than a knockout.

"Who knows? With the right fight, the right timing, the right network, maybe I'll throw some bows again.

"There's a couple of good girls, but I don't want to get ahead of myself. I haven't done MMA in a couple of years, but it would be an honour to go in there with the best, just to showcase my skills.

"I've learned a lot throughout the years in MMA. I'm not perfect yet, but I have these hands with four-ounce gloves."

articles.title: Alejandra Boixader sigue haciendo historia y se proclama Campeona del Mundo juvenil de MMA
articles.standfirst: Ya fue campeona de Europa a principio de año
articles.summary: Ya fue campeona de Europa a principio de año
articles.body: No hay quien la pare. Alejandra Boixader ha cerrado un impresionante jueves en Belgrado y se ha proclamado Campeona del Mundo de MMA amateur tras ganar a la ucraniana Anhelina Kovinova por sumisión vía kata gatame. Es la nueva campeona del mundo juvenil IMMAF en la categoría Youth B de 62 kilos. La peleadora barcelonesa, que ya se proclamó Campeona de Europa a principio de año en su debut en las artes marciales mixtas, ha tenido la mejor transición posible desde el jiu-jitsu: dos campeonatos, dos oros y siete finalizaciones por sumisión en siete peleas. Que en categoría amateur no se pueda golpear en la cara favorece estos inicios suyos y saca a relucir su 'background' de élite en el suelo. Alejandra, hija del ex peleador y ahora entrenador Ray Boixader, ya es una eminencia en el jiu-jitsu pese a no haber cumplido la mayoría de edad: es seis veces campeona Mundial de jiu-jitsu.

articles.title: El combate entre Hokit y Pereira, cada vez más cerca
articles.standfirst: El entrenador de 'Poatan' ve con buenos ojos el enfrentamiento, mientras que el estadounidense ha pedido al brasileño o a Ciryl Gane
articles.summary: El entrenador de 'Poatan' ve con buenos ojos el enfrentamiento, mientras que el estadounidense ha pedido al brasileño o a Ciryl Gane
articles.body: El pasado 14 de junio, el UFC Casa Blanca fue el escenario de consagración para Josh Hokit como una de las próximas estrellas de peso pesado tras noquear a Derrick Lewis. A su vez, también fue un día amargo para Alex Pereira, ya que perdió en su debut en peso pesado ante Ciryl Gane por K.O. y de paso la oportunidad de obtener el título interino. Semanas previas a ese evento, Hokit intentó provocar a Pereira y así forzar un beef para un futuro enfrentamiento, y a día de hoy está más cerca que nunca que ambos se vean las caras. En un principio, 'Poatan' solo estaba interesado en una revancha con Gane al considerar a Hokit un rival con mucho menos status y legado que el suyo. Lo que está claro es que Alex no quiere volver a bajar a peso semipesado, y al darse cuenta que la UFC quiere unificar los cinturones entre Ciryl Gane y Tom Aspinall -campeón indiscutido- está obligado a buscar otro oponente. Por tanto, su entrenador y amigo Glover Teixeira ha reconocido que no vería con malos ojos un duelo entre su pupilo y el peleador más controversial de la UFC después de todo lo que le ha insultado. "Estoy seguro de que Alex va a conseguir ese cinturón, se va a quedar en peso pesado. Hokit está hablando mucha mierda... Ve ahí, noquéale y vuelve al top, y después obten la revancha con Gane", sentenció Glover en una entrevista con Ariel Helwani. La respuesta de Hokit no se hizo esperar para sorpresa de nadie, aunque puso algún que otro condicionante para verse las caras con 'Poatan'. "O me dan a Ciryl por el título o a Alex por el cinturón BMF. Estoy harto de ver a estos 'olfateadores de entrepiernas' que se limitan a defenderse y rezar, y a que la gente los llame BMF o P4P. articles.title: Chris Billam-Smith expects Jai Opetaia showdown in 2027 | 'I’m on it. And I’m still getting better!'
articles.summary: Chris Billam-Smith believes he will secure a shot at leading cruiserweight Jai Opetaia in 2027, as long as they keep winning; Billam-Smith expects to fight again before the end of the year, and is open to a fight with an old amateur rival, Cheavon Clarke
articles.body:
Chris Billam-Smith expects to fight Jai Opetaia next year, if they are both victorious in their upcoming bouts.

Former world champion Billam-Smith has long targeted Australia's Opetaia, widely regarded as the best cruiserweight in the sport.

Opetaia will box Noel Mikaelian on the undercard of Conor Benn's fight with Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas on September 12.

  • Fisher opponent revealed ahead of Copper Box return
  • Richards to face Kalajdzic showdown on Fisher bill
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

Billam-Smith should fight again before the end of the year and then intends to resume his pursuit of Opetaia.

It's a showdown he believes will happen in 2027.

"I think so. I think I need to get through my next fight and then I'll fight the winner of that, whoever that might be," Billam-Smith told Sky Sports.

"Mikaelian on his day is a good fighter but I pick Jai to beat him.

"But it might take him a few rounds to set the pace and obviously Mikaelian's got some good names on his record, has some good performances but I feel like he's slowed down a little bit and gone a little bit past it now."

For his return to action Billam-Smith said: "Looking most probably around November time.

"I think it will be London or Bournemouth. Don't know who yet.

"The champions seem a bit tied up, I think [David] Benavidez is lining up a fight for December as well in Vegas, I believe."

Cheavon Clarke caught the eye with a knockout, comeback victory over Jack Massey on the undercard of Billam-Smith's barnstorming battle with Ryan Rozicki.

"Obviously Chev won on my undercard. He's got two [amateur] wins over me so from a competitor's point of view I'd very much like to get one back," Billam-Smith noted, speaking to Sky Sports at a screening of new boxing drama Fightland.

"[Clarke-Massey was] a superb fight which I think was definitely going to win fight of the night - until our fight."

Both Clarke and Massey were amateur foes of Billam-Smith's, and both of them beat the Bournemouth man in elite championship finals.

He wants revenge. "I owe him one and I feel like that does the Jack Massey one in the ABA final as well. Both of those have beaten me in an ABA final. That would put that to bed so that would be nice," Billam-Smith said.

"I'm up for whoever," he added. "Zuffa are signing people all the time so you just don't know who's going to pop up out the woodwork and get offered. So we will see on that front."

Billam-Smith lost his WBO championship to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and beat Brandon Glanton in his only bout of last year. But June's thunderous collision with Rozicki showed that the 36-year-old can still perform in top-level contests.

"I think if I'd taken my foot off the gas and was just sort of coasting I would definitely have been beat that night. I think that's the important thing to take away from my point of view," Billam-Smith said.

"I had to be switched on and pushing the training as I do and looking for different ways to improve.

"I'm on it. And I'm still getting better."

Fightland is coming to Sky and NOW on August 27.

articles.title: Tyson Fury claims Anthony Joshua fight in serious doubt after his British rival asked 'for more money'
articles.summary: Tyson Fury has cast doubts over the Anthony Joshua fight after claiming on social media his British rival has asked for 'more money'; Fury and Joshua have been negotiating a fight that could happen in November at Madison Square Garden in New York
articles.body:
Tyson Fury has claimed his fight against Anthony Joshua is now in serious doubt after his British heavyweight rival asked for 'more money'.

Fury and Joshua have been holding talks about staging their long-awaited fight in November, with Madison Square Garden in New York emerging as the likely location.

But Fury has suggested in a social media video the blockbuster bout could fall through due to Joshua's request for a bigger fight purse.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

Sky Sports understands Joshua has signed a contract for the fight and Matchroom are still working towards an announcement.

"Quick update for you. It doesn't look like they are going to sign the fight and it doesn't look like it is going to happen all because [Joshua's promoter] Eddie Hearn and that want more money," Fury said.

"They have already had that much money off Turki (Alalshikh) over the last few years Eddie and AJ, they have had boxing deals, they have had darts deals, they have had snooker deals, they have had everything.

"And yet, they have got the audacity and cheek of flea-bitten rats to ask for more money from old Turki that you have had combined over the last couple of years.

"Keep on running you cowards."

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has confirmed the original fight contract stipulated that the bout would be staged in the UK.

Matchroom Boxing CEO Frank Smith had told Sky Sports earlier this week it was a 'critical week' for negotiations but he was optimistic about an agreement.

"It will be disappointing for it not to be in the UK, but at the same time if it means seeing the fight, we all want to see that fight happen," said Smith. "Let's see how things play out.

"We're following the terms of what we signed up to right now, which is a fight in the UK. That is what we signed up to and when the fight was announced in March, April time, the fight was signed, those were the terms we signed up for.

"They are the conversations really that are taking place right now. MSG is a proposed venue that they would like to look at, i.e The Ring Magazine, Saudi delegation, so let's see.

"I think November is possible. Later in November is possible, but again the next seven to 10 days, a lot of progress has got to be made in order to make that happen to get [fighters] into camp to give yourself that eight-to-10-week period, a dedicated camp away from all the promotional obligations."

Joshua and Fury were unable to agree terms in 2021 and fight plans fell apart after a US judge ruled Fury had to face Deontay Wilder in a trilogy fight instead.

Fury's manager Spencer Brown has told Sky Sports he was uneasy about the delay in announcing the Joshua fight.

"Everybody's got a bit of doubt in their mind," he said. "There's reasons you could think that.

"If you'd asked me a week ago, I'd have said no, but now it's a little bit concerning that things haven't progressed down the line. We need to get this fight on."

articles.title: Amanda Serrano survives Lucrecia Manzur scare to seal 50th win but all-time KO record eludes her
articles.summary: Amanda Serrano retained her WBA and WBO featherweight titles with a majority-decision win in Temecula, California; the 38-year-old becomes one of the few women in history to reach 50 professional victories but stays level with Christy Martin on 32 knockouts
articles.body:
Amanda Serrano survived a bruising examination from Lucrecia Manzur to claim the 50th win of her professional career, retaining her WBA and WBO featherweight titles by majority decision.

Two judges scored it 116-112 for the Puerto Rican in the main event of Most Valuable Promotions' show, which was broadcast live on TikTok, with the third returning a 114-114 draw.

Victory brought Serrano (50-4-1) a milestone few in the women's game have ever reached, but the night's other target got away. She needed a stoppage to break the all-time women's knockout record she shares with Christy Martin, but Serrano was taken the full 12 rounds and stays on 32.

  • Latest boxing headlines, reports, highlights and interviews
  • Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
  • Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract

She was made to work for the half-century too.

Manzur (14-5), fighting outside her native Argentina for the first time, pressed forward from the opening bell and opened a cut on Serrano's forehead in the fourth round, appearing to stun the champion more than once as she built an early lead.

The 27-year-old finished the more accurate fighter, connecting at 34 per cent overall to Serrano's 25 according to CompuBox before Serrano's furious rally over the closing rounds swung the fight back to the champion, whose hand was injured along the way.

Serrano said: "A tough, young fighter. She was hungry. And I knew that coming into training.

"I just love being a woman in this sport and helping women's boxing grow beautifully."

Manzur, whose five-fight winning run was ended, was gracious in defeat.

"Tonight was a dream come true," said through a translator. "Thanks to you, you really helped put female boxing on a pedestal."

On the record that got away, Serrano added: "We still got that 33rd knockout, I've got one more fight. If I don't get it, I'm glad that I tied with Christy Martin.

Martin, watching from ringside, had given her blessing before the first bell.

"I'm always in her corner," she said. "No matter what, I'm always in her corner."

Could Serrano fight again? Legend weighs up options after epic career

The first woman to win world titles in seven divisions, Serrano turned professional in 2009 and her trilogy with Katie Taylor twice filled Madison Square Garden and became a landmark for the sport.

She said in April that this would probably be her final year, and has long wanted a farewell fight in Puerto Rico but no opponent has yet been finalised, so the Manzur bout might spell the end of Serrano's boxing career.

Serrano later admitted on X the fight had been "rough" and suggested she now has a decision to make with her team about how her career ends.

"The mind tells you one thing but the body does another," she wrote. "You can fight anyone you want and squeeze out a victory but Father Time isn't allowing too much of that."

Although this may be the end of her career in the ring it might not the end of her involvement in combat sports, with the 37-year-old open to building on her three-fight MMA career.

"Well, I am undefeated in MMA," Serrano said, before Friday night's bout. "I'm 2-0-1, with two submissions.

"I love the knockouts, but I think I love submissions a lot more. It's a lot more fun to get a submission than a knockout.

"Who knows? With the right fight, the right timing, the right network, maybe I'll throw some bows again.

"There's a couple of good girls, but I don't want to get ahead of myself. I haven't done MMA in a couple of years, but it would be an honour to go in there with the best, just to showcase my skills.

"I've learned a lot throughout the years in MMA. I'm not perfect yet, but I have these hands with four-ounce gloves."

articles.summary: Rolly Romero continued a big-game hunting campaign in boxing's welterweight division, but he came up short in defense of his WBA 147-pound title against Teofimo Lopez and dropped a majority decision at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

articles.title: Former World Champion Boxer Zolani Tete Killed in South Africa
articles.summary: JOHANNESBURG, South Africa (AP) — Former world champion boxer Zolani Tete has been shot and killed at his home in South Africa, government officials said Friday.
articles.body:
JOHANNESBURG, South Africa (AP) — Former world champion boxer Zolani Tete has been shot and killed at his home in South Africa, government officials said Friday.

Gayton McKenzie, South Africa's sports, arts and culture minister, said the 38-year-old Tete was killed in his car and that a 27-year-old woman who was in the vehicle with him was shot multiple times and is in hospital.

Tete held world title belts in the WBF flyweight category from 2007-2008 and the WBO bantamweight title in 2017 and 2019.

Police said the shooting took place at Mdantsane, Eastern Cape and that Tete was arriving at his residence and waiting for the gate to open when he was ambushed by two armed suspects wearing balaclavas.

articles.summary: Amanda Serrano was unable to break the record for most knockout wins by a female boxer, but she still made history with her 50th career win over Lucrecia Manzur on Friday night.
articles.body:
Amanda Serrano was unable to break the record for most knockout wins by a female boxer, but she still made history with her 50th career win over Lucrecia Manzur on Friday night.

Serrano, who was defending the WBO and WBA featherweight titles, held on for a majority decision victory against Manzur that the judges scored 116-112, 116-112 and 114-114.

ESPN's Michael Rothstein noted the 50-win milestone is "a benchmark that few women's fighters have reached."

Even though Serrano got the win, she acknowledged the impressive showing by Manzur.

"A tough, young fighter. She was hungry," Serrano said in the ring. "And I knew that coming into training."

In a post on X following the event, Serrano also hinted that this could be the last fight of her storied career.

Serrano entered the fight with 32 career knockout wins, tied with Christy Martin for the most ever by a women's boxer.

Even though Serrano was unable to surpass Martin's KO mark, the win did move her ahead of the Hall of Famer in the victory column. Martin finished her legendary career with a 49-7-3 record.

"We still got that 33rd knockout [to try for]; I've got one more fight," Serrano said after the fight (h/t Rothstein). "If I don't get it, I'm glad that I tied with Christy Martin."

The fight was much closer than anticipated with Manzur having a strong argument as the winner.

Serrano landed more total punches (168-164) and power punches (142-118), but Manzur was more efficient overall with a 33.9 percent hit rate on total punches compared to 24.9 percent for the champ.

Manzur landed more total strikes in seven of the 12 rounds, but Serrano connected on more power punches in seven rounds, including each of the last four rounds.

This was just the second time in Serrano's career she won a fight by majority decision. The only other time it happened was her first professional bout against Jackie Trivilino in March 2009.

Serrano has a recent loss by majority decision against Katie Taylor in July 2025 in the final fight of their historic trilogy. The 37-year-old has rebounded with three consecutive victories since that defeat.

If this does end up being the last fight of Serrano's career, she will go down as one of the most accomplished boxers in the history of the sport. Her accolades include a Guinness World Record for winning world titles in seven different weight classes.
